title: Murchadh Beag takes Eòghann mac Pheadair from the coal-face
summary: The old scribe of Taigh na Fèithe, Murchadh Beag, hears a coal-breaker's young son recite back a whole day's cartage without once looking at the board, and asks the boy's father whether a household might spare him for a scribe's stool. Eòghann mac Pheadair is set to sweep Taigh na Fèithe floor and mix ink before he is let touch a leaf.

title: Taigh na Fèithe's leaf takes in the rope-ground sown with barley
summary: Eòghann mac Pheadair, fourteen and newly trusted with a leaf of his own, enters the ground given up by Cuan shean's rope-walks for barley, the first entry he copies whose full sense Murchadh Beag has to explain to him. He learns that a scribe's business is the fact and the year, not the grief behind it.

title: A household of Cnoc chaol removes its gallery-claim from the shore
summary: After the great wave that took two children from the beach at Cnoc chaol, the household of one of the drowned strikes itself from its old gallery and takes up a new claim further from the water. Eòghann mac Pheadair enters the removal on Taigh na Fèithe's leaf the following season, cold and plain as he was taught.

title: Eòghann mac Pheadair witnesses the market bounds at Baile Mòr dhìreach
summary: Sent east on his own feet for the first time, Eòghann mac Pheadair stands witness for Na Seachd Taighean when the crown's grant of a market is read at Baile Mòr dhìreach and its boundary stones set. He watches the first stalls go up the same afternoon and walks the road home slower than he walked out.

title: Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves
summary: A scribe of An Talla Dearg's own household, Mòrag nic Ìomhair, rides the thirty-nine miles to Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg to set the crown's reckoning of Bliadhnaichean an Diosail against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own, after the two offices' counts are found not to agree. The master of Taigh na Fèithe grants her the book for as many days as the matter takes.

title: The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended
summary: Working three days by lamplight, Eòghann mac Pheadair and Mòrag nic Ìomhair trace the two offices' counts of An Diosal back to a single year, early after An Diosal, entered twice by one office's habit or once by the other's. Neither leaf either scribe has brought can say which office erred, or whether either truly has.

title: The two counts settled by agreement, not by proof
summary: Taigh na Fèithe and the crown's scribe take the crown's count for the reckoning that will go forward, since it touches more households than Taigh na Fèithe's own, and Eòghann mac Pheadair writes Taigh na Fèithe's agreement to it in his own hand. The master of Taigh na Fèithe's mark is set under his, and the crown scribe's office mark under that.

title: The day of Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh fixed
summary: The same agreement that settles the count also fixes, for the first time, a single day on which Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh is to be kept by every harbour of the coast together, in place of each keeping it a day or two either side of its neighbours by its own old custom. Mòrag nic Ìomhair carries word of it down to Seann Skell.

title: The agreement-leaf folded into Leabhar a' Chùraim
summary: Eòghann mac Pheadair keeps his copy of the sealed agreement between two older leaves of Leabhar a' Chùraim that had never before had a stranger's mark folded in among them. He tells the master of Taigh na Fèithe only that the crown's scribe was a hard woman to argue a figure past and an easy one to agree a figure with.

title: The coast keeps the rite on the agreed day
summary: Mòrag nic Ìomhair writes to Eòghann mac Pheadair the following winter that not a single harbour of the coast has written to complain of the day set for Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh. Eòghann keeps the short note folded inside his own working leaves for the rest of his working life.

title: Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe
summary: A rider carries north country talk to Taigh na Fèithe of a house of disputation newly founded at Inis mhòr, whose first master refuses every answer offered him on whether the vein answers any true count of years or only the custom of counting it. Eòghann mac Pheadair, old now, hears it out and goes back to his leaf.

title: The master of Taigh na Fèithe stands for Eòghann at the crowning
summary: When Na Seachd Taighean' custodians go down to Cathair dhearg to see the new queen crowned, as the compact requires, the master of Taigh na Fèithe goes in place of Eòghann mac Pheadair, whose legs will no longer answer for a journey of thirty-nine miles in a single season. Eòghann hears the crowning described to him afterward by the returning master.

title: Eòghann mac Pheadair is carried to the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
summary: In the last cold turn of the year, his chest gone tight in a way no winter before has managed, Eòghann mac Pheadair lets himself be carried by cart to the rebuilt bath-house below Muileann ruadh, where he sits in the warm water among coal-breakers, salt-carriers and a shepherd's widow, none of them minding whose gallery the others answer to.

title: Eòghann mac Pheadair shows the agreement-leaf to his own pupil
summary: Asked by the young scribe he has lately taken to teaching what the finest thing was that he ever did in a life spent mostly at a stool, Eòghann mac Pheadair unfolds the thirty-year-old agreement-leaf and tells the boy it was not the count that made it worth keeping, but the honest agreement written under it.

title: Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona
summary: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty after seven-and-thirty years crowned, and the heir, two-and-forty years old, is crowned the same season.

title: Eòghann mac Pheadair at four-and-twenty
summary: At four-and-twenty Eòghann mac Pheadair has old Murchadh Beag's stool at Taigh na Fèithe as good as his own, and enters the wave at Cnoc chaol on the general leaf as he enters every disaster that touches a household of the coal-right: names, place, day.

title: Birth of Eilidh Bhàn
summary: A girl, Eilidh, fair enough to be called Eilidh Bhàn from her first year, is born at Cathair dhearg, granddaughter of the ruler who has then held the hall nine-and-twenty years.

title: Death of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
summary: The fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at nine-and-eighty after seven-and-forty years crowned, and the crown passes to a granddaughter, Eilidh Bhàn, eighteen years old.
